citations.title: The Barpeta Satra was founded by Shri Shri Madhaba Deva, the great Vaisnavite poet and reformer and the chief apostle of Shri Shri Sankar Deva in the 15th century. It is a premier religious place not only for the district but also for the entire north-eastern region. This is the nerve centre of Assamese vaisnavite religion and culture. The famous and beautiful feature of the Satra is its “Kirtan ghar” (congregation prayer hall). The “Kirtanghar” was built according to size and style of “Brindabani Cloth”. At the request of Chilaraya the brother of Ahom king Naranarayan Shri Shri Sankar Deva had woven this cloth by the weavers of Tatikich (Barpeta) at Patbausi depicting the early activities of Krishna to the killing of Kangsha and was presented to Chilaraya. The king in turn, had gifted Sankar Deva with Rup (money). The length and breath of the Kirtan ghar is 120’ fts and 60 fts respectively. It is worth mentioning here that there are two huge posts of Tulshi trees each measuring 22’ in hight and 9’ in circumference just at the entrance of the Kirtan ghar supporting the structure along with other concrete pillars. The Akshya Banti (an oil lamp) is said to have been lit by Shri Madhabadeva at the time of beginning of the Satra which is kept continuously burning before the alter in the Bhaj ghar of the Kirtan ghar. In the prayer hall, there are three Guru Akhans made of wood with various design. These three Guru Akhans are in the name of Shri Shri Sankardev, Shri Madhabadeva and Shri Mathura Das Bura Ata. In the walls of the Kirtan ghar, various kinds of images of Gods and Goddesses taken from different religions books are carved and illuminated beautifully. A journey to Barpeta Satra is a holy pilgrimage for all Hindu people.
